"Neuralink has given me back my voice."

Terry has ALS. It was slowly taking his speech. He had to retire from a career he loved, and one of his wife's biggest fears was losing the ability to talk with him.

Now, in Neuralink's VOICE trial, he thinks the words and hears them spoken out loud. Then he told her: "I love you."

Audrey was paralyzed from the neck down in a car accident. For 20 years she couldn't write her name. The first time she signed it with her mind, it looked like her real handwriting.

Think about how incredible this is.

🎥 @neuralink

Sri Lanka considers Starlink for remote health facilities after Cyclone Ditwah.

* Uva Province health authorities proposed Starlink to restore reliable connectivity at remote facilities and offices.
* Cyclone Ditwah damaged cellular networks and disrupted emergency coordination.
* Starlink previously donated 145 terminals and provided free service to affected users after the disaster.

Satellite internet is becoming a critical backup when traditional networks go down.

Tomorrow morning: Starship Flight 14 goes for orbit.

Window opens Mon Sep 28 at 5:15 a.m. PT (7:15 a.m. CT) for 75 minutes from Starbase. After 13 suborbital flights, this is SpaceX's first attempt to put Starship into orbit.

• 26 Starlink V3 satellites — first V3s into the constellation (~26 Tbps capacity added)
• ~6 orbits at ~275 km, then Pacific splashdown west of Chile
• Mission clock: nearly 10 hours

MOST PEOPLE THINK EARTH IS THE ENERGY CEILING

"I'd say you're an extremely kick-ass civilization if you get to 1% of the Sun's energy. And I'm like, wow, that civilization's going to be vastly more powerful than us, to say the least."
— @elonmusk

Right now we harness almost none of our star's power. Even the sunlight that hits Earth is only about half a billionth of what the Sun puts out.

• Today — <<1 trillionth of the Sun (not even Kardashev Type I yet)
• Aspiration — even a millionth of the Sun (>1,000× Earth's max possible)
• 1% of the Sun — a civilization vastly more powerful than us

Starship moves the tonnage.
Orbital solar captures the watts.
Type II is the destination.
